stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // VAMPIRE

//L3Harris

📍Melbourne, FL

Tech: Counter-drone strike

Platform: Portable vehicle kit

Goal: Defeat drones and remotely piloted platforms for the U.S. Navy's littoral defense needs.

Why: The kit can be installed on most vehicles with a cargo bed and launches APKWS or other laser-guided munitions.

Ticker: NYSE: LHX

Traction: Selected by the U.S. Navy to deliver VAMPIRE counter-unmanned systems, and delivering VAMPIRE systems to the U.S. Army, per L3Harris.

VAMPIRE, short for Vehicle-Agnostic Modular Palletized ISR Rocket Equipment, is a self-contained weapons solution that combines reconnaissance and precision strike. L3Harris says it meets the Navy's requirements for littoral counter-unmanned systems defense, and the company is engineering new capabilities and ruggedizing the system for maritime conditions.

L3Harris also unveiled its Wraith Shield software earlier this year. The radio-as-a-sensor software can be incorporated with VAMPIRE and Drone Guardian systems to add layered defense against unmanned threats.

Source: L3Harris Technologies, 08SEP26

Image: L3Harris (courtesy)

fields.headline: PARAVISION WINS UP TO $6.5M STATE DEAL
fields.deck: The award is for digital identity assurance, and records do not name the products bought.

stories.caption:
A federal contract with Paravision, a facial recognition developer, has a potential value of up to $6.5 million. The State Department awarded it on September 23 and initially obligated $1.3 million. The firm-fixed-price deal can run through September 22, 2031. It was competed under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside, and only one offer came in.

Procurement records tag the work as "digital detection/identity assurance." Award records do not list which Paravision products were bought, but the wording lines up with the company's tools for spotting manipulated and AI-generated faces. Paravision sells facial recognition, passive liveness detection and deepfake detection. Its Deepfake Detection product checks still images and video frames for digital manipulation, and the company has widened it to catch fully synthetic faces made with diffusion models and generative adversarial networks.

The public record does not show whether the award covers deepfake detection, liveness detection, facial recognition or other software. A separate $24,717 purchase order for a "purchase card for software license" was awarded to the company on April 30. Public records do not identify that software or show whether the April buy was a test, pilot or precursor to the September contract.

Source: Biometric Update, 17OCT26

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and other unauthorized vessel ingress, in support of U.S. maritime border security.

Why: The vessels are solar powered and capable of multi-month endurance on station, so they can keep watch for long periods.

Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Lightfish vessels have operated on the Rio Grande since January 2026 in support of federal border security efforts, and a fleet has been deployed in the Gulf of America, per Seasats.

Seasats says each Lightfish is roughly 11 feet long and weighs about 340 pounds. Its payload bay can swap between cameras, signals gear and sonar, and earlier missions have used electro-optical, infrared, signals and sonar payloads. Two people can launch and recover the boats from a ramp or a pickup bed.

The Gulf deployment widens a surveillance effort that Seasats has run under the Homeland Defense office of the Assistant Secretary of War. It follows the company's earlier work supporting Operation River Wall on the southern border. Seasats says it holds over $100 million in U.S. government contracts.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, 2 Oct 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Spc. Jacob D. Harrell

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

media.credit: U.S. Army photo by Spc. Jacob D. Harrell

MISSION BRIEF // X10D

//Skydio

Tech: EW resilience

Platform: Small UAS

Goal: Keep small drones flying and returning when GPS and communications are jammed or spoofed.

Why: Vision-based navigation and return flights are meant for GNSS-denied environments, according to the company.

Traction: Listed as on the Blue UAS Cleared list, per Skydio.

Skydio describes the X10D as an sUAS built for EW resilience and survivability on the toughest battlefields. The company says it can keep its connection through GPS and communication jamming, switch channels with a multiband radio, and use Anchor Points to navigate and return autonomously without GPS. Its VT300-Z and VT300-L sensor packages include a Teledyne FLIR Boson+ thermal camera, which the company says is the first thermal sensor of its kind on a small UAS.

The page lists a top speed of 45 mph, a deployment time under 40 seconds, IP55 dust and water protection, NDAA compliance, and AES 256 encryption. Gust handling is rated to 28.6 mph and the service ceiling to 15,000 ft.

Source: Skydio, undated product page (skydio.com/x10d)

Image: skydio.com (courtesy)

stories.caption:
Three MilCityUSA stories from the past week, in one quick brief.

Microchip Technology acquired Austin-based VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors and its HARDSIL process technology to Microchip's space and defense portfolio. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Lockheed Martin unveiled PAC-3 Edge, its entry in the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor competition. The company says the interceptor adds a new seeker, a Northrop Grumman multi-pulse rocket motor and upgraded flight controls, with testing planned for 2027 and deployment targeted by 2031.

The Florida National Guard ran Drone Crucible 26.3, an integration test with joint partners at Camp Blanding from Sept. 26 to Oct. 2. The Guard reported combining Tactical Assault Kit location data, unmanned-system information and video feeds into a shared operational picture.

Source: Florida National Guard via army.mil, Oct. 6, 2026.
